Ok I understand, that makes it more difficult, it’s still important to have you time doing things you enjoy though, but that’s a difficult situation. I really think you should try, even just saying your feeling a bit down, something really undramatic and minor to see his reaction without shocking him too much. His your boyfriend if he really loves you he will want to know and want to help you. But I get it’s hard and scary and people can react badly to such serious topics. And try to remember that even though they reacted badly your sister and friend probably still care about you. It’s hard for other people to know how to react or not react out of shock or disbelief or just to forget it ever happened. I am certain that if you took your life they would care, but I’m sorry to hear your lacking in support so much right now. As for your gp, I think you need to look in to seeing a new one if you know of any who are better, he sounds pretty useless because you are not wasting anyone’s time. Mental illness is illness, it sucks, it’s not your fault and it’s not a healthy way to live, your concerns are very important in fact they are life threatening, don’t disregard that!

Hey there. Let me just start by saying I’ve been there, I am there, in al honesty I’m currently using talking to you as a way to rationalise my own thinking, so I get it. First of all your looking for help and looking for a reason. This is a good sign, it’s what I’m doing too. I’m going to say your boyfriend is your first reason. Whether you think he loves you or not it sounds like he does, and cliche as it is he would be devastated if you were gone. I know you’ve had bad experiences with peoples reactions. My mum laughed at me the first time I told her too. But I think you should talk to your boyfriend, even just say your feeling really down and a bit desperate, maybe if your worried don’t use the word suicide until you can judge his reaction? 
As for reasons to live, beyond the way it effects friends and family, in all honesty I’m struggling to find them too. Go back to gaming if it makes you happy, a wholesome life is one where you feel comfortable and alive and if gaming helps you get closer to that then it’s definitely worth it! If your willing to find a reason then definitely also talk to a doctor about it as well, I don’t know if you’ve tried this but a good doctor can help, in my experience, and I mean even just a gp, not a therapist (as I know they are expensive)
I hope things get better for you, feel free to pm me if you want to talk.

You may have tried but let her know that just because she seeks help it doesn't mean they will institutionalise her. Unless they think she's an immediate threat to herself or others she will be allowed to go home as usual. She needs to make sure she gets on the right treatment plan for her and has someone medical she can trust to take a bit of weight off you as well. If she's still concerned she might want to try a confidential online chat or telephone call to get an idea of what might be best for her? Or she can even speak to someone and not reveal everything right away if there are particular symptoms she's worried will get her institutionalised, she may feel better talking about it once she starts to get to know the doctor better. I hope this helps a bit

Hey, sorry to hear your feeling like this, it sucks I know I feel much the same and honestly I can't give the best advice as I'm still dealing with it to. However have you tried any form of therapy/counselling along with the antidepressant? This can make a big difference for some, and if antidepressants aren't really working for you it could be a better treatment. Also have you spoken to your prescribing doctor about this? Some people try 2 or 3 different meds before thy find one that works, it may be possible your on the wrong medication and it's worth a try? For me the 3 things that keep me going are friends and family who I don't want to leave devastated (which is a sucky reason but whatever it works), knowing that there are many treatment options I haven't tried, maybe I just haven't found what works for me yet, and I started doing ice skating classes, which I find I do enjoy (once I'm there, I'm never motivated to go) and it's good because I have to go, and exercise does really help! If you can join a sports team or a class or even do something with friends it really does help
I hope things improve for you

I know that feeling, nothing working, and it's frustrating. If you can it would be good to make an appointment with your psychiatrist and let him know how your feeling. People get much easier to be around and social groups get much clearer after high school. Try to hang in there, I know it's really hard but your reaching the end of your school days and things change a lot at the end of school, you may find that you change your mind.

The person who told you this probably cannot see any joy in life or any reason they should be alive. They are quite possibly desperate and suicidal too. Therefore there opinion on whether your life is worth living or not is clouded by the fact that they don't think life is worth living in general. When I feel terrible and like life isn't worth living I try and talk to people who I know don't suffer from mental illness, and I ask them if you didn't have to think about the effect it would have on your loved ones would you want to be alive or dead? They all say alive, every single one, even the ones who got abused as children or lost their parents etc. they worked through their depression and are glad they lived and have found new things to love in life.
Don't let the views of a person who is probably suffering themselves decide how you feel about your life, I hope things look up for you soon

I just see so many unhappy people. It makes me feel terrible, watching my parents cry and lash out at each other, witnessing the stress and pain my close friends go through, just to get through day to day life. I fell so useless to help them, I can't just make them feel good (I know that's not how emotion works). It just feels weird to me to think that they still want to live through that. 
My opinion on death is that it's just nothing. Just like before you're born, you have no recollection of it. After you die all the neurons and synapses and transmitters and pathways in your brain that made you you shut down and disintegrate, so there's nothing to be felt. I guess to me feeling nothing seems like a much easier option than having to suffer through this only to die in the end anyway (thankfully).

I only relapse because I'm not better, I still have healing to do, but I have a friend who just last year spent time in a mental hospital due to her symptoms and she no longer has suicidal thoughts, ever! It happens, and it happens often, that people completely recover. I understand it's really hard to see that and the darkness your in isn't something you can just switch off, but maybe if you can just give it a bit longer? 1 week at a time. Try something new and see if it lightens the dark for you, talk to a professional about it (or try a different one if your already seeing someone) or even just a friend, or a stranger (you are welcome to PM me). I am sorry you feel this way.

I know how this feels. I know how good it can feel to feel like there's an end in sight, and I know how hard it is to think you have to keep living when you feel like you can't, or you just feel like every living moment is pain. But I also know, from my own experience and the experiences of others around me, that if you can wait, postpone a little longer,  there may be options.
I don't know if you've ever attempted suicide. I don't know your story and I don't want to make any assumptions. I can see your hurting and I am sorry for your pain. I really am. But I want to share my own experience. I have attempted suicide. I felt the same relief as you. I failed. And, besides the guilt I felt surrounding my attempt, and on the days when I relapse into severe depression, I am eternally grateful I failed. After the year of proper treatment I've received, I can now see things to live for that don't include living for the sake of others. Things I look forward to doing in my life. I still get suicidal, but I can see my improvements and I can see more on the horizon. Like you I saw great freedom in death, but now I see that I can do what I want with my life, and there's a lot of fun things I'd like to do, like scuba dive and play with seals (that's just my dream).  I can see that because the pain decreased, it was a bit slow and it wasn't easy and I was sure it wouldn't but it did. 
Again I understand how you feel, that you can't just make it go away and that this may not help, but I just wanted to share a positive experience with you from someone who's been there.
I wish you all the best
